name: Sherlock Holmes
hook: Baker Street's consulting detective: the deerstalker, the pipe, Moriarty, and a hound on the moor.

facts.label: Arthur Conan Doyle
facts.statement: Arthur Conan Doyle, born in 1859 and knighted in 1902, modeled Holmes on his teacher Dr. Joseph Bell, a master of diagnostic deduction.

facts.label: Sherlock Holmes
facts.statement: Sherlock Holmes lives at 221B Baker Street; more than 60 actors have played him, with Basil Rathbone the definitive for many.

facts.label: the deerstalker
facts.statement: The deerstalker cap came from illustrator Sidney Paget, not Conan Doyle; Basil Rathbone wore one as Holmes.

facts.label: Dr. Watson
facts.statement: Dr. Watson, the good-natured physician who narrates the stories, marries Mary Morstan in "A Scandal in Bohemia".

facts.label: Professor Moriarty
facts.statement: Professor Moriarty is Holmes's great adversary, "one of the greatest brains of the century"; they plunge together at the Reichenbach Falls in Switzerland.

facts.label: A Study in Scarlet
facts.statement: A Study in Scarlet (1887) introduced Holmes, opening with a chapter titled "Mr. Sherlock Holmes" and a murder at Lauriston Gardens.

facts.label: The Hound of the Baskervilles
facts.statement: The Hound of the Baskervilles describes a huge, luminous, spectral creature on the moor and remains the most famous Holmes book.
